recommended_tables.table_name: Sustainability risk taxonomy and control mapping
suggested_columns: Where it manifests (value chain / business activities)
recommended_tables.notes: Keep entries descriptive and non-quantitative unless the company can substantiate metrics. Use consistent phrasing across rows.

recommended_tables.table_name: Roles and responsibilities (three lines of defence)
recommended_tables.notes: Use generic role types (e.g., business owners, risk oversight, internal audit/independent assurance) rather than named teams.

recommended_tables.table_name: Climate scenario and data inventory (method transparency)
recommended_tables.notes: Avoid naming specific scenario providers or regulators; refer to “recognized scenario frameworks” and “external guidance” where applicable.
Do not hard-code cadence; describe triggers or typical periodicity only if substantiated.

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.description: A simple flow diagram showing identification → assessment/scoring → due diligence → review/approval → monitoring/reporting → feedback loop into framework updates.
A conceptual diagram showing business ownership, risk oversight, and independent assurance, including key handoffs and escalation points.
A diagram mapping upstream, own operations, and downstream risk touchpoints, indicating where key controls are applied.
A process diagram showing data inputs → scenario variables → modelling/projections → risk outputs → monitoring and governance review.

required_narrative_blocks: Scope definition: clarify what is covered in this section (sustainability risks within enterprise risk management) and what is addressed elsewhere.
Integration statement: explain how sustainability and climate risks are embedded into existing governance and risk processes rather than managed in a parallel system.
Governance and accountability: describe roles across lines of defence, including who owns the framework, who implements controls, and who provides independent review/assurance.
Lifecycle description: outline how risks are identified, assessed (including criteria), managed (controls/mitigations), monitored, and escalated.
Risk theme structure: for each material risk theme, provide a consistent mini-template (risk → concentration/why it matters → mitigations → controls/assurance).
Exception handling: explain how deviations from policies/guidelines are documented, approved, and monitored.
Climate deep-dive rationale: explain why climate-related risks are treated as a distinct disclosure topic and how they connect to financial risk considerations.
Method transparency (for climate): describe scenario analysis approach, data categories, modelling workflow at a high level, and how outputs inform decisions.
Monitoring and continuous improvement: describe reporting artifacts, review triggers, and how the framework is updated as regulations, data, and practices evolve.
optional_narrative_blocks: Segment/vertical tailoring: explain how risk management differs by business segment or activity type, using a consistent structure per segment.
Controls in action callout: a short boxed summary of the assessment/scoring methodology and factor categories considered.
Value-chain due diligence: describe third-party/vendor assessment approach and procurement controls as part of risk coverage.
Data limitations and roadmap: a transparent statement of current gaps and planned enhancements to data, tools, and coverage.
output_structure_rules: Use hierarchical headings that reflect scope and lifecycle (overview, value-chain coverage, internal operations, climate deep-dive) rather than outcomes.
Maintain a consistent sequence for each risk theme: definition/risk statement → relevance and concentration → management actions → controls/assurance → monitoring/escalation.
Use bullet lists for layered controls and for methodology components; avoid long narrative blocks without signposting.
Separate present practice from planned enhancements using explicit qualifiers (e.g., “currently,” “in this reporting period,” “planned”).
Avoid entity-specific labels; use generic role types and generic references to recognized frameworks and external guidance.
Ensure every control claim is paired with an evidence artifact type (policy, procedure, training, audit, monitoring report) or clearly marked as planned.
